raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

This PR adds request-local windowed hidden-state capture for rollouts. Consumers can request hidden states for selected response positions instead of collecting the full response.

The MRV2 optimization copies captured rows asynchronously into pinned CPU memory and reuses output completion synchronization to make the results ready before they are returned.

Implements the windowed capture contract discussed in #56916.

## Key results

- Window capture reduces GPU-to-CPU transfer volume by 93.75% in the measured workload.
- With CUDA graphs enabled, window capture achieves **1.0858x throughput on Qwen3.5-0.8B** and a **1.1033x median paired speedup on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**, compared with full-response capture in the same optimized implementation.
- **21 GPU tests passed**, including CUDA Graph output-buffer reuse and completion synchronization.

## Validation

### Qwen3.5-0.8B — CUDA Graph benchmark

**Tested commit:** `5d4cf1e560f645068d8cb49a53c1d381fe58122e` (optimized implementation and GPU regression tests). The complete benchmark script and reproduction commands are provided below.

Configuration: RTX 3090, Qwen3.5-0.8B, BF16, TP=PP=DP=1, CUDA graphs enabled, synchronous scheduling, and prefix caching disabled. Each request has 512 input and 512 output tokens. The benchmark runs 128 requests in batches of 16, with two measured rounds after warmup. The requested response window is `[128, 160)`.

| Capture mode | Generation + export, median [min, max] (s) | Output tokens/s | D2H per request |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Disabled | 23.68 [23.62, 23.74] | 2767.97 | 0 |
| Full response | 25.97 [25.87, 26.06] | 2524.01 | 1 MiB |
| Window `[128, 160)` | 23.91 [23.86, 23.97] | 2740.44 | 64 KiB |
| Window beyond response length | 23.91 [23.86, 23.96] | 2740.76 | 0 |

Compared with full-response capture, window capture reduces D2H transfer from **1 MiB to 64 KiB per request (−93.75%)** and improves generation-plus-export throughput by **1.0858x**. Its elapsed time is also within approximately **1%** of capture-disabled execution.

Both capture modes export the same 32 hidden-state rows as Base64. Full capture first transfers the complete response to CPU; window capture transfers only the requested rows. The benchmark measures generation and CPU export after warmup, using the same workload and implementation for all four modes.

#### Correctness

- **21 hidden-state capture tests passed on GPU**, including six CUDA Graph buffer-reuse cases across three capture layouts and two event-wait policies. These verify output readiness and captured-state integrity across buffer reuse.
- **Correctness checks passed:** all four capture modes produced identical generated tokens, and full/window captured hidden states had a **maximum absolute difference of 0** on the checked batch.
- **GPU synchronization check passed** for all four modes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.
- **Static checks passed:** Ruff, formatting, and `git diff --check`.

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — CUDA Graph benchmark

**Correctness checks passed.** These measurements extend the performance evaluation to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash using PR source `5d4cf1e560`.

#### Configuration

- **Hardware environment:** two GB200 nodes, four GPUs per node, 184.3 GiB per GPU.
- **Model execution:** TP=4, PP=1, BF16 activations, and the model's original FP8/FP4 weights.
- **Software:** CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3, and the nightly image built at 06:15 UTC with its native extensions.
- **Workload:** 512 input tokens and 512 output tokens per request; batch size 16; 128 requests; capture window `[128, 160)`.
- **Measurement:** one warmup batch per mode, followed by five measured rounds. CUDA graphs were enabled; prefix caching and async scheduling were disabled. Elapsed time includes generation and export.

#### Results

The table shows the median across five rounds. D2H volume is reported for the returning TP rank.

| Capture mode | Generation + export (s) | Output tokens/s | D2H per request | TTFT P95 (ms) | Token ITL P95 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Disabled (Off) | 51.087 | 1282.83 | 0 | 187.16 | 12.69 |
| Full response (Full) | 56.778 | 1154.25 | 5 MiB | 191.97 | 14.29 |
| Window `[128, 160)` (Window) | 51.450 | 1273.78 | 320 KiB | 187.72 | 13.28 |
| Window beyond response length (Never) | 51.208 | 1279.79 | 0 | 186.69 | 12.89 |

Window capture achieved a **1.1033x median paired speedup over full-response capture**, equivalent to approximately **10.3% higher throughput**. Its median paired elapsed-time overhead relative to capture-disabled execution was **0.89%**.

These paired statistics are calculated within each round, then summarized by their median. Ratios calculated directly from the elapsed-time medians in the table are **1.1036x** for Full/Window and **0.71%** for Window overhead relative to Off.

#### Profiling

| Metric | Full response | Window `[128, 160)` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| D2H volume per request, summed across all TP ranks | 20 MiB | 1.25 MiB |
| CPU export time per request | 0.191 ms | 0.187 ms |
| CPU copy allocation and submission time per request | 11.111 ms | 0.693 ms |
| GPU copy execution time per 16-request batch, summed across GPUs | 87.71 ms | 5.46 ms |

Window capture reduced D2H data volume by **93.75%**. GPU copy execution times above are sums across GPUs, rather than wall-clock batch times.

A supplementary eager experiment used three rounds with 16 requests per mode and produced a **0.9985x median paired Full/Window speedup**. The throughput improvement above was observed with CUDA graphs enabled.

### Qwen3.5-0.8B reproduction

Check out commit `5d4cf1e560f645068d8cb49a53c1d381fe58122e`, install that vLLM version in `.venv`, and save the complete script below as `benchmarks/benchmark_hidden_state_capture.py`:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
uv run --no-sync --python .venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/benchmark_hidden_state_capture.py \
  --model /path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B \
  --input-tokens 512 \
  --output-tokens 512 \
  --window-start 128 \
  --window-size 32 \
  --batch-size 16 \
  --requests 128 \
  --rounds 2 \
  --result capture_graph.json
```

The script requires CUDA, checks generated tokens and selected hidden states, prints metrics for each round, and writes raw measurements and configuration metadata to JSON. CUDA graphs remain enabled; add `--enforce-eager` for a separate eager comparison.

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project

"""GPU rollout benchmark for PR #57736; same-version full vs window capture.

Run from an editable PR checkout on a CUDA Linux host:
    uv run --no-sync --python .venv/bin/python \
        benchmarks/benchmark_hidden_state_capture.py --model Qwen/Qwen3-8B

Uses fixed-size request batches to compare capture modes under a reproducible
workload. Both capture modes export the same selected window as Base64.
The benchmark records generation, export, and host-copy overhead separately.
"""

import argparse
import base64
import json
import os
import random
import statistics
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from time import perf_counter

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD", "spawn")

import numpy as np
import torch

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.v1.hidden_state_capture import HiddenStateCapturePlan

SCENARIOS = ("off", "full", "window", "never")


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="Qwen/Qwen3-8B")
    parser.add_argument("--input-tokens", type=int, default=512)
    parser.add_argument("--output-tokens", type=int, default=512)
    parser.add_argument("--window-start", type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument("--window-size", type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=16)
    parser.add_argument("--requests", type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=5)
    parser.add_argument("--warmup-waves", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=("bfloat16", "float16"), default="bfloat16")
    parser.add_argument("--gpu-memory-utilization", type=float, default=0.85)
    parser.add_argument("--enforce-eager", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1234)
    parser.add_argument("--atol", type=float, default=0.02)
    parser.add_argument("--rtol", type=float, default=0.02)
    parser.add_argument("--result", type=Path, default=Path("capture_benchmark.json"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    for name in (
        "input_tokens",
        "output_tokens",
        "window_size",
        "batch_size",
        "requests",
        "rounds",
        "warmup_waves",
    ):
        if getattr(args, name) <= 0:
            parser.error(f"--{name.replace('_', '-')} must be positive")
    if (
        not 0
        <= args.window_start
        < args.window_start + args.window_size
        <= args.output_tokens
    ):
        parser.error("the window must lie inside the generated response")
    if args.requests % args.batch_size:
        parser.error("--requests must be divisible by --batch-size")
    return args


def plans_for(scenario, count, args):
    if scenario == "off":
        return None
    if scenario == "full":
        start, end = 0, args.output_tokens
    elif scenario == "window":
        start, end = args.window_start, args.window_start + args.window_size
    else:
        start = args.output_tokens + 128
        end = start + args.window_size
    return [
        HiddenStateCapturePlan.from_window(
            request_id=f"bench-{i}",
            prompt_len=args.input_tokens,
            start=start,
            end=end,
            collection_id="gpu-benchmark",
            coordinate="response",
            min_rows=end - start,
        )
        for i in range(count)
    ]


def selected_states(output, scenario, args):
    capture = output.hidden_state_capture
    if scenario in ("off", "never"):
        if capture is not None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{scenario}: unexpected captured result")
        if (
            scenario == "never"
            and output.hidden_capture_skip_reason != "ended_before_window"
        ):
            raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected skip: {output.hidden_capture_skip_reason}")
        return None
    if capture is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"capture failed: {output.hidden_capture_skip_reason}")
    if capture.hidden_states.device.type != "cpu" or capture.copied_bytes <= 0:
        raise RuntimeError("expected actual GPU-to-CPU capture")
    start = args.input_tokens - 1
    if scenario == "full":
        expected = np.arange(start, start + args.output_tokens)
        rows = capture.hidden_states[
            args.window_start : args.window_start + args.window_size
        ]
    else:
        start += args.window_start
        expected = np.arange(start, start + args.window_size)
        rows = capture.hidden_states
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(capture.hidden_positions, expected)
    if capture.hidden_states.shape[0] != len(expected):
        raise RuntimeError("hidden-state row count does not match positions")
    return rows


def generate(llm, prompts, params, plans):
    return llm.generate(prompts, params, hidden_state_capture=plans, use_tqdm=False)


def validate(llm, prompts, params, args):
    reference_tokens = None
    reference_states = None
    max_error = 0.0
    for scenario in SCENARIOS:
        outputs = generate(
            llm, prompts, params, plans_for(scenario, len(prompts), args)
        )
        tokens = [list(out.outputs[0].token_ids) for out in outputs]
        if any(len(ids) != args.output_tokens for ids in tokens):
            raise RuntimeError("generation did not produce the requested token count")
        if reference_tokens is None:
            reference_tokens = tokens
        elif tokens != reference_tokens:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{scenario}: generated tokens differ from capture-off")
        rows = [selected_states(out, scenario, args) for out in outputs]
        if scenario == "full":
            reference_states = [row.clone() for row in rows]
        elif scenario == "window":
            for actual, expected in zip(rows, reference_states):
                torch.testing.assert_close(
                    actual, expected, atol=args.atol, rtol=args.rtol
                )
                max_error = max(
                    max_error, (actual.float() - expected.float()).abs().max().item()
                )
        del outputs, rows
    print(
        f"Correctness PASS: all scenarios, batch={len(prompts)}, "
        f"max_abs_error={max_error:.6g}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return {"batch_size": len(prompts), "max_abs_error": max_error}


def run_round(llm, prompts, params, scenario, args, round_id):
    plans = plans_for(scenario, args.batch_size, args)
    generation_s = export_s = 0.0
    copied_bytes = copy_wait_ms = encoded_bytes = 0
    ttft_ms, mean_itl_ms = [], []
    for offset in range(0, len(prompts), args.batch_size):
        wave = prompts[offset : offset + args.batch_size]
        started = perf_counter()
        outputs = generate(llm, wave, params, plans)
        generation_s += perf_counter() - started

        # Validate outside the measured generation and export regions.
        for out in outputs:
            count = len(out.outputs[0].token_ids)
            if count != args.output_tokens:
                raise RuntimeError(f"expected {args.output_tokens} tokens, got {count}")
            selected_states(out, scenario, args)
            if out.metrics is None or out.metrics.first_token_ts <= 0:
                raise RuntimeError("missing engine timing metrics")
            stats = out.metrics
            ttft_ms.append(stats.first_token_latency * 1000)
            if count > 1:
                mean_itl_ms.append(
                    (stats.last_token_ts - stats.first_token_ts) * 1000 / (count - 1)
                )
            if out.hidden_state_capture is not None:
                copied_bytes += out.hidden_state_capture.copied_bytes
                copy_wait_ms += out.hidden_state_capture.copy_ms

        # Same final window and encoding work for full and window capture.
        started = perf_counter()
        if scenario in ("full", "window"):
            for out in outputs:
                states = out.hidden_state_capture.hidden_states
                if scenario == "full":
                    states = states[
                        args.window_start : args.window_start + args.window_size
                    ]
                byte_view = states.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).numpy()
                encoded = base64.b64encode(memoryview(byte_view))
                encoded_bytes += len(encoded)
                del encoded
        export_s += perf_counter() - started
        del outputs

    total_s = generation_s + export_s
    return {
        "round": round_id,
        "scenario": scenario,
        "generation_s": generation_s,
        "generation_plus_export_s": total_s,
        "generation_output_tokens_s": args.requests * args.output_tokens / generation_s,
        "end_to_end_output_tokens_s": args.requests * args.output_tokens / total_s,
        "ttft_p95_ms": float(np.percentile(ttft_ms, 95)),
        "per_request_mean_itl_p95_ms": float(np.percentile(mean_itl_ms, 95))
        if mean_itl_ms
        else None,
        "d2h_mib_per_request": copied_bytes / args.requests / 2**20,
        "copy_wait_ms_per_request": copy_wait_ms / args.requests,
        "cpu_export_ms_per_request": export_s * 1000 / args.requests,
        "base64_bytes_per_request": encoded_bytes / args.requests,
    }


def git_head():
    try:
        return subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
            cwd=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1],
            text=True,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        ).strip()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return "unknown"


def main():
    args = parse_args()
    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.version.cuda is None:
        raise SystemExit("This benchmark requires an NVIDIA CUDA GPU and CUDA PyTorch.")
    import vllm

    metadata = {
        "args": {
            key: str(val) if isinstance(val, Path) else val
            for key, val in vars(args).items()
        },
        "git_head": git_head(),
        "vllm": vllm.__version__,
        "torch": torch.__version__,
        "cuda": torch.version.cuda,
        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),
        "gpu_memory_gib": torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 2**30,
        "environment": {
            key: value
            for key, value in os.environ.items()
            if key
            in (
                "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES",
                "VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD",
                "VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT",
                "VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER",
                "VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND",
                "VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK",
                "CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING",
            )
        },
        "scope": (
            "TP=1 PP=1; fixed-size batches; final hidden state; "
            "Base64 encoding of selected window"
        ),
        "copy_timer_scope": (
            "Host-side allocation/submission for async capture; "
            "blocking capture also includes any associated wait"
        ),
    }
    print(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2), flush=True)
    llm = LLM(
        model=args.model,
        dtype=args.dtype,
        seed=args.seed,
        tensor_parallel_size=1,
        pipeline_parallel_size=1,
        max_model_len=args.input_tokens + args.output_tokens + 16,
        max_num_seqs=args.batch_size,
        gpu_memory_utilization=args.gpu_memory_utilization,
        async_scheduling=False,
        enable_prefix_caching=False,
        enforce_eager=args.enforce_eager,
        disable_log_stats=False,
    )
    tokenizer = llm.get_tokenizer()
    source = tokenizer.encode(
        "Explain how GPUs accelerate matrix multiplication and model inference. "
        "Give several examples and continue with technical details. ",
        add_special_tokens=False,
    )
    if not source:
        raise RuntimeError("tokenizer produced an empty prompt")
    prompts = []
    for i in range(args.requests):
        shift = i % len(source)
        rotated = source[shift:] + source[:shift]
        ids = (rotated * ((args.input_tokens + len(rotated) - 1) // len(rotated)))[
            : args.input_tokens
        ]
        prompts.append({"prompt_token_ids": ids})
    params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0,
        max_tokens=args.output_tokens,
        min_tokens=args.output_tokens,
        ignore_eos=True,
        detokenize=False,
    )
    correctness = validate(llm, prompts[: args.batch_size], params, args)
    for scenario in SCENARIOS:
        print(f"Warmup: {scenario}", flush=True)
        for _ in range(args.warmup_waves):
            outputs = generate(
                llm,
                prompts[: args.batch_size],
                params,
                plans_for(scenario, args.batch_size, args),
            )
            del outputs

    print(
        "\nround scenario  gen_s    total_s   tok/s     TTFTp95  meanITLp95  "
        "D2HMiB/req  copy_host_ms/req  export_ms/req",
        flush=True,
    )
    records = []
    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
    for round_id in range(1, args.rounds + 1):
        order = list(SCENARIOS)
        rng.shuffle(order)
        for scenario in order:
            row = run_round(llm, prompts, params, scenario, args, round_id)
            records.append(row)
            itl = row["per_request_mean_itl_p95_ms"]
            itl_text = f"{itl:.3f}" if itl is not None else "N/A"
            print(
                f"{round_id:5d} {scenario:8s} {row['generation_s']:8.3f} "
                f"{row['generation_plus_export_s']:9.3f} "
                f"{row['end_to_end_output_tokens_s']:9.2f} "
                f"{row['ttft_p95_ms']:8.3f} {itl_text:>10s} "
                f"{row['d2h_mib_per_request']:11.4f} "
                f"{row['copy_wait_ms_per_request']:17.3f} "
                f"{row['cpu_export_ms_per_request']:13.3f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            args.result.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            args.result.write_text(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "metadata": metadata,
                        "correctness": correctness,
                        "records": records,
                    },
                    indent=2,
                ),
                encoding="utf-8",
            )

    print("\nSummary: median [min, max] across rounds", flush=True)
    for scenario in SCENARIOS:
        rows = [row for row in records if row["scenario"] == scenario]
        for key in (
            "generation_plus_export_s",
            "end_to_end_output_tokens_s",
            "d2h_mib_per_request",
        ):
            values = [row[key] for row in rows]
            print(
                f"{scenario:8s} {key:30s} {statistics.median(values):.4f} "
                f"[{min(values):.4f}, {max(values):.4f}]"
            )
    speedups = []
    for round_id in range(1, args.rounds + 1):
        by_mode = {row["scenario"]: row for row in records if row["round"] == round_id}
        speedups.append(
            by_mode["full"]["generation_plus_export_s"]
            / by_mode["window"]["generation_plus_export_s"]
        )
    print(
        "\nWindow vs full, median paired total-time speedup: "
        f"{statistics.median(speedups):.4f}x",
        flush=True,
    )
    print(f"Raw results saved to: {args.result.resolve()}", flush=True)
    print("meanITLp95: P95 of per-request mean ITL.")
    print("copy_wait_ms_per_request: measured host-side copy overhead.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

## Details

MRV2 queues D2H copies into fresh pinned CPU buffers. The existing AsyncOutput completion event ensures that copying finishes before those buffers are read. Other capture-helper callers retain the blocking default.

For single-GPU synchronous scheduling with CUDA graphs enabled, the implementation uses non-sleeping output-event waits. Other configurations retain sleeping waits. Completion is still checked before results are consumed.

All four benchmark modes use the same output-event wait policy, making the full-versus-window comparison consistent. The optimized path combines selective D2H transfer with the MRV2 copy/synchronization improvements.

The Qwen3.5-0.8B benchmark uses a single GPU; the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash benchmark uses TP=4 and PP=1. Both use synchronous scheduling with CUDA graphs enabled.

### Related work

Related PRs #57663 and #59543 explore complementary hidden-state capture paths. This PR focuses on request-local response windows and efficient MRV2 export; shared interfaces and transfer mechanisms can be aligned during review.

## 第一性原理：审计所采用的必要契约

R1. 对 L 个 prompt token，第 j 个生成 token 由 h[L-1+j] 预测。因此 response [a,b) 对应 absolute [L-1+a,L-1+b)。这里返回的是预测该 response token 的 hidden state，不是消耗该 token 后的下一位置状态。RFC #56916 明确规定这一语义。
R2. 一个实际 forward 的第 i 个请求占用 query_start_loc[i:i+2] 指定的行，其绝对起点为该 forward 开始前的 computed token 数。必须先对所有请求推进 row offset，再按各自窗口取交集；不能按采集请求重新紧密编号。
R3. speculative forward 可以产生未被接受的候选 row。GPU 先按窗口复制，scheduler 再按实际交付的 token 区间过滤；同一 mask 必须用于 positions 和 states。
R4. CPU payload 可读必须晚于 D2H 完成，且 graph output 在覆盖前必须完成读取。MRV2 当前在 main stream 排队复制，output-copy stream wait_stream(main_stream) 后记录 event，get_output 同步 event，建立传递的 happens-before。blocking=True/False 不改变这个就绪契约。
R5. 每个请求独立拥有 plan/buffer；窗口完成和请求终止需要清理 worker plan。输出结果不得因为 DELTA coalescing、内部 ID 改写或 FINAL_ONLY 延迟而丢失。
R6. 校验对象必须是实际执行的参数；不支持的组合应明确拒绝或返回说明，不能先校验另一份参数再执行不兼容请求。
R7. copied_bytes/copy_ms 是提交或执行过的复制开销，不应因 row 后来被过滤、重算或没有新 token 而消失。有效 row 数和复制开销是不同指标。
R8. capture 未开启时不应引入无关调度、模型输出或全局等待策略变化；性能优化需要对应 feature-off 和 CPU 开销证据。

与 RFC 对照：响应坐标、半开窗口、稀疏 hidden_positions 为准、短样本/min_rows、request-local 状态等设计有合理依据。aux capture 只复用模型已有 speculative aux outputs，不能采任意未配置层；PCP/DCP、async scheduling、adaptive verification、encoder-decoder 均被拒绝。以上是支持范围，不是全组合通过证明。

frozen plan 防止同批请求共享计划后被原地重写；replace 是重新绑定 request_id 所需，而不是冗余复制大 tensor。
finished_hidden_capture_req_ids 与 finished_req_ids 生命周期不同：窗口可以在 generation 结束前完成；不能简单合并成只有 finished_req_ids。
query_start_loc 的验证防止 prompt-logprob batch 实际行边界错配；不能用“采集请求每请求一行”的假设替代。
accepted positions/state 同 mask、去重和显式 sparse positions 支持 speculative rejection、短结果与 replay；不要用连续 arange 填补实际缺失 row。
pinned CPU buffer + non_blocking copy 与 output event 传递同步是 Graph buffer reuse 正确性的必要组合；不能只删除 event wait 来换吞吐。

[P2] Finalize capture when a stop string ends the request in the frontend

Capture is finalized in the scheduler only when its window completes or the scheduler observes the request stopping. A stop string is detected later in this output processor: it emits a finished response and aborts EngineCore. If generation stops inside the capture window, the scheduler's buffered rows are discarded without `finish()`, including a partial capture that satisfies `min_rows`. The finished response can therefore contain neither a capture nor a skip reason. A CPU output-processor probe confirms the stop-string path returns `finished=True`, both capture fields unset, and the request in `reqs_to_abort`.

Please coordinate capture finalization with frontend stop handling, or explicitly reject capture with stop strings until that combination is supported. Add a regression test that stops inside the window after meeting `min_rows`, and distinguish it from EOS/max-token termination.

Follow-up review of `6f9e63baaf`.

The source changes address the four issues from my previous review: capture completion now uses accepted output progress; stop strings and streaming input are explicitly rejected at admission; and auxiliary-layer errors are retained until a normal output is emitted. The scheduler regressions, CPU CI wiring, removal of the unused state enum, and extraction of buffer finalization are also improvements. This is source-level verification, not a claim that I reran the updated tests.

I would still like the following evidence and design alignment before approval:

The standalone GPU script was removed without a replacement real-model numerical comparison. Please provide a small reference comparison and feature-off/mixed-batch coverage, including speculative rejection and pipeline parallelism where support is claimed. If that matrix cannot be validated yet, narrow the initially supported combinations.

Please report comparable throughput, TTFT and ITL for the baseline, capture unused, and the periods before/during/after the window. RFC #56916 specifically asks for outside-window overhead measurements. The current `11 passed, 3 deselected` helper result does not establish numerical correctness or acceptable serving overhead; please identify the deselected tests and explain why they were excluded. I am not asserting a measured slowdown without benchmark data.

## Overview

This PR adds request-local windowed hidden-state capture for rollouts. Consumers can request hidden states for selected response positions instead of collecting the full response.

The MRV2 optimization copies captured rows asynchronously into pinned CPU memory and reuses output completion synchronization to make the results ready before they are returned.

Implements the windowed capture contract discussed in #56916.

## Key results

- Window capture reduces GPU-to-CPU transfer volume by 93.75% in the measured workload.
- With CUDA graphs enabled, window capture achieves **1.0858x throughput on Qwen3.5-0.8B** and a **1.1033x median paired speedup on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**, compared with full-response capture in the same optimized implementation.
- **21 GPU tests passed**, including CUDA Graph output-buffer reuse and completion synchronization.

## Validation

### Qwen3.5-0.8B — CUDA Graph benchmark

**Tested commit:** `5d4cf1e560f645068d8cb49a53c1d381fe58122e` (optimized implementation and GPU regression tests). The complete benchmark script and reproduction commands are provided below.

Configuration: RTX 3090, Qwen3.5-0.8B, BF16, TP=PP=DP=1, CUDA graphs enabled, synchronous scheduling, and prefix caching disabled. Each request has 512 input and 512 output tokens. The benchmark runs 128 requests in batches of 16, with two measured rounds after warmup. The requested response window is `[128, 160)`.

| Capture mode | Generation + export, median [min, max] (s) | Output tokens/s | D2H per request |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Disabled | 23.68 [23.62, 23.74] | 2767.97 | 0 |
| Full response | 25.97 [25.87, 26.06] | 2524.01 | 1 MiB |
| Window `[128, 160)` | 23.91 [23.86, 23.97] | 2740.44 | 64 KiB |
| Window beyond response length | 23.91 [23.86, 23.96] | 2740.76 | 0 |

Compared with full-response capture, window capture reduces D2H transfer from **1 MiB to 64 KiB per request (−93.75%)** and improves generation-plus-export throughput by **1.0858x**. Its elapsed time is also within approximately **1%** of capture-disabled execution.

Both capture modes export the same 32 hidden-state rows as Base64. Full capture first transfers the complete response to CPU; window capture transfers only the requested rows. The benchmark measures generation and CPU export after warmup, using the same workload and implementation for all four modes.

#### Correctness

- **21 hidden-state capture tests passed on GPU**, including six CUDA Graph buffer-reuse cases across three capture layouts and two event-wait policies. These verify output readiness and captured-state integrity across buffer reuse.
- **Correctness checks passed:** all four capture modes produced identical generated tokens, and full/window captured hidden states had a **maximum absolute difference of 0** on the checked batch.
- **GPU synchronization check passed** for all four modes with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.
- **Static checks passed:** Ruff, formatting, and `git diff --check`.

### DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — CUDA Graph benchmark

**Correctness checks passed.** These measurements extend the performance evaluation to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash using PR source `5d4cf1e560`.

#### Configuration

- **Hardware environment:** two GB200 nodes, four GPUs per node, 184.3 GiB per GPU.
- **Model execution:** TP=4, PP=1, BF16 activations, and the model's original FP8/FP4 weights.
- **Software:** CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3, and the nightly image built at 06:15 UTC with its native extensions.
- **Workload:** 512 input tokens and 512 output tokens per request; batch size 16; 128 requests; capture window `[128, 160)`.
- **Measurement:** one warmup batch per mode, followed by five measured rounds. CUDA graphs were enabled; prefix caching and async scheduling were disabled. Elapsed time includes generation and export.

#### Results

The table shows the median across five rounds. D2H volume is reported for the returning TP rank.

| Capture mode | Generation + export (s) | Output tokens/s | D2H per request | TTFT P95 (ms) | Token ITL P95 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Disabled (Off) | 51.087 | 1282.83 | 0 | 187.16 | 12.69 |
| Full response (Full) | 56.778 | 1154.25 | 5 MiB | 191.97 | 14.29 |
| Window `[128, 160)` (Window) | 51.450 | 1273.78 | 320 KiB | 187.72 | 13.28 |
| Window beyond response length (Never) | 51.208 | 1279.79 | 0 | 186.69 | 12.89 |

Window capture achieved a **1.1033x median paired speedup over full-response capture**, equivalent to approximately **10.3% higher throughput**. Its median paired elapsed-time overhead relative to capture-disabled execution was **0.89%**.

These paired statistics are calculated within each round, then summarized by their median. Ratios calculated directly from the elapsed-time medians in the table are **1.1036x** for Full/Window and **0.71%** for Window overhead relative to Off.

#### Profiling

| Metric | Full response | Window `[128, 160)` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| D2H volume per request, summed across all TP ranks | 20 MiB | 1.25 MiB |
| CPU export time per request | 0.191 ms | 0.187 ms |
| CPU copy allocation and submission time per request | 11.111 ms | 0.693 ms |
| GPU copy execution time per 16-request batch, summed across GPUs | 87.71 ms | 5.46 ms |

Window capture reduced D2H data volume by **93.75%**. GPU copy execution times above are sums across GPUs, rather than wall-clock batch times.

A supplementary eager experiment used three rounds with 16 requests per mode and produced a **0.9985x median paired Full/Window speedup**. The throughput improvement above was observed with CUDA graphs enabled.

### Qwen3.5-0.8B reproduction

Check out commit `5d4cf1e560f645068d8cb49a53c1d381fe58122e`, install that vLLM version in `.venv`, and save the complete script below as `benchmarks/benchmark_hidden_state_capture.py`:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
uv run --no-sync --python .venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/benchmark_hidden_state_capture.py \
  --model /path/to/Qwen3.5-0.8B \
  --input-tokens 512 \
  --output-tokens 512 \
  --window-start 128 \
  --window-size 32 \
  --batch-size 16 \
  --requests 128 \
  --rounds 2 \
  --result capture_graph.json
```

The script requires CUDA, checks generated tokens and selected hidden states, prints metrics for each round, and writes raw measurements and configuration metadata to JSON. CUDA graphs remain enabled; add `--enforce-eager` for a separate eager comparison.

    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=("bfloat16", "float16"), default="bfloat16")
    parser.add_argument("--gpu-memory-utilization", type=float, default=0.85)

    parser.add_argument("--rtol", type=float, default=0.02)

    if args.requests % args.batch_size:
        parser.error("--requests must be divisible by --batch-size")
    return args


def plans_for(scenario, count, args):
    if scenario == "off":
        return None
    if scenario == "full":
        start, end = 0, args.output_tokens
    elif scenario == "window":
        start, end = args.window_start, args.window_start + args.window_size
    else:
        start = args.output_tokens + 128
        end = start + args.window_size
    return [
        HiddenStateCapturePlan.from_window(
            request_id=f"bench-{i}",
            prompt_len=args.input_tokens,
            start=start,
            end=end,
            collection_id="gpu-benchmark",
            coordinate="response",
            min_rows=end - start,
        )
        for i in range(count)
    ]


def selected_states(output, scenario, args):
    capture = output.hidden_state_capture
    if scenario in ("off", "never"):
        if capture is not None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{scenario}: unexpected captured result")
        if (
            scenario == "never"
            and output.hidden_capture_skip_reason != "ended_before_window"
        ):
            raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected skip: {output.hidden_capture_skip_reason}")
        return None
    if capture is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"capture failed: {output.hidden_capture_skip_reason}")
    if capture.hidden_states.device.type != "cpu" or capture.copied_bytes <= 0:
        raise RuntimeError("expected actual GPU-to-CPU capture")
    start = args.input_tokens - 1
    if scenario == "full":
        expected = np.arange(start, start + args.output_tokens)
        rows = capture.hidden_states[
            args.window_start : args.window_start + args.window_size
        ]
    else:
        start += args.window_start
        expected = np.arange(start, start + args.window_size)
        rows = capture.hidden_states
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(capture.hidden_positions, expected)
    if capture.hidden_states.shape[0] != len(expected):
        raise RuntimeError("hidden-state row count does not match positions")
    return rows


def generate(llm, prompts, params, plans):
    return llm.generate(prompts, params, hidden_state_capture=plans, use_tqdm=False)


def validate(llm, prompts, params, args):
    reference_tokens = None
    reference_states = None
    max_error = 0.0
    for scenario in SCENARIOS:
        outputs = generate(
            llm, prompts, params, plans_for(scenario, len(prompts), args)
        )
        tokens = [list(out.outputs[0].token_ids) for out in outputs]
        if any(len(ids) != args.output_tokens for ids in tokens):
            raise RuntimeError("generation did not produce the requested token count")
        if reference_tokens is None:
            reference_tokens = tokens
        elif tokens != reference_tokens:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{scenario}: generated tokens differ from capture-off")
        rows = [selected_states(out, scenario, args) for out in outputs]
        if scenario == "full":
            reference_states = [row.clone() for row in rows]
        elif scenario == "window":
            for actual, expected in zip(rows, reference_states):
                torch.testing.assert_close(
                    actual, expected, atol=args.atol, rtol=args.rtol
                )
                max_error = max(
                    max_error, (actual.float() - expected.float()).abs().max().item()
                )
        del outputs, rows
    print(
        f"Correctness PASS: all scenarios, batch={len(prompts)}, "
        f"max_abs_error={max_error:.6g}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return {"batch_size": len(prompts), "max_abs_error": max_error}


def run_round(llm, prompts, params, scenario, args, round_id):
    plans = plans_for(scenario, args.batch_size, args)
    generation_s = export_s = 0.0
    copied_bytes = copy_wait_ms = encoded_bytes = 0
    ttft_ms, mean_itl_ms = [], []
    for offset in range(0, len(prompts), args.batch_size):
        wave = prompts[offset : offset + args.batch_size]
        started = perf_counter()
        outputs = generate(llm, wave, params, plans)
        generation_s += perf_counter() - started

        # Validate outside the measured generation and export regions.
        for out in outputs:
            count = len(out.outputs[0].token_ids)
            if count != args.output_tokens:
                raise RuntimeError(f"expected {args.output_tokens} tokens, got {count}")
            selected_states(out, scenario, args)
            if out.metrics is None or out.metrics.first_token_ts <= 0:
                raise RuntimeError("missing engine timing metrics")
            stats = out.metrics
            ttft_ms.append(stats.first_token_latency * 1000)
            if count > 1:
                mean_itl_ms.append(
                    (stats.last_token_ts - stats.first_token_ts) * 1000 / (count - 1)
                )
            if out.hidden_state_capture is not None:
                copied_bytes += out.hidden_state_capture.copied_bytes
                copy_wait_ms += out.hidden_state_capture.copy_ms

        # Same final window and encoding work for full and window capture.
        started = perf_counter()
        if scenario in ("full", "window"):
            for out in outputs:
                states = out.hidden_state_capture.hidden_states
                if scenario == "full":
                    states = states[
                        args.window_start : args.window_start + args.window_size
                    ]
                byte_view = states.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).numpy()
                encoded = base64.b64encode(memoryview(byte_view))
                encoded_bytes += len(encoded)
                del encoded
        export_s += perf_counter() - started
        del outputs

    total_s = generation_s + export_s
    return {
        "round": round_id,
        "scenario": scenario,
        "generation_s": generation_s,
        "generation_plus_export_s": total_s,
        "generation_output_tokens_s": args.requests * args.output_tokens / generation_s,
        "end_to_end_output_tokens_s": args.requests * args.output_tokens / total_s,
        "ttft_p95_ms": float(np.percentile(ttft_ms, 95)),
        "per_request_mean_itl_p95_ms": float(np.percentile(mean_itl_ms, 95))
        if mean_itl_ms
        else None,
        "d2h_mib_per_request": copied_bytes / args.requests / 2**20,
        "copy_wait_ms_per_request": copy_wait_ms / args.requests,
        "cpu_export_ms_per_request": export_s * 1000 / args.requests,
        "base64_bytes_per_request": encoded_bytes / args.requests,
    }


def git_head():
    try:
        return subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
            cwd=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1],
            text=True,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        ).strip()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return "unknown"

    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.version.cuda is None:

    print(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2), flush=True)
    llm = LLM(
        model=args.model,
        dtype=args.dtype,
        seed=args.seed,
        tensor_parallel_size=1,
        pipeline_parallel_size=1,
        max_model_len=args.input_tokens + args.output_tokens + 16,
        max_num_seqs=args.batch_size,
        gpu_memory_utilization=args.gpu_memory_utilization,
        async_scheduling=False,
        enable_prefix_caching=False,
        enforce_eager=args.enforce_eager,
        disable_log_stats=False,
    )
    tokenizer = llm.get_tokenizer()
    source = tokenizer.encode(

    if not source:

    prompts = []
    for i in range(args.requests):

    for scenario in SCENARIOS:

        for _ in range(args.warmup_waves):

    for scenario in SCENARIOS:
        rows = [row for row in records if row["scenario"] == scenario]
        for key in (
            "generation_plus_export_s",

## Details

MRV2 queues D2H copies into fresh pinned CPU buffers. The existing AsyncOutput completion event ensures that copying finishes before those buffers are read. Other capture-helper callers retain the blocking default.

For single-GPU synchronous scheduling with CUDA graphs enabled, the implementation uses non-sleeping output-event waits. Other configurations retain sleeping waits. Completion is still checked before results are consumed.

All four benchmark modes use the same output-event wait policy, making the full-versus-window comparison consistent. The optimized path combines selective D2H transfer with the MRV2 copy/synchronization improvements.

The Qwen3.5-0.8B benchmark uses a single GPU; the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash benchmark uses TP=4 and PP=1. Both use synchronous scheduling with CUDA graphs enabled.

### Related work

Related PRs #57663 and #59543 explore complementary hidden-state capture paths. This PR focuses on request-local response windows and efficient MRV2 export; shared interfaces and transfer mechanisms can be aligned during review.

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class HiddenStateCapturePlan:
+    request_id: str
+    prompt_len: int
+    window_start_abs: int
+    window_end_abs: int
+    collection_id: str
+    min_rows: int = 1
+    aux_layer_ids: tuple[int, ...] = ()
+    hidden_layout: str = "final"
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if (
+            self.prompt_len < 1
+            or self.window_start_abs < self.prompt_len - 1
+            or self.window_start_abs >= self.window_end_abs
+            or self.min_rows < 1
+            or self.min_rows > self.window_end_abs - self.window_start_abs
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Invalid hidden-state capture plan")
+        if self.hidden_layout not in ("final", "aux_final", "dflash_aux"):
+            raise ValueError("Invalid hidden-state layout")
+        if bool(self.aux_layer_ids) != (self.hidden_layout != "final"):
+            raise ValueError("Hidden-state layout does not match auxiliary layers")
+        if len(set(self.aux_layer_ids)) != len(self.aux_layer_ids):
+            raise ValueError("Duplicate auxiliary hidden-state layers")
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_window(
+        cls,
+        request_id: str,
+        prompt_len: int,
+        start: int,
+        end: int,
+        collection_id: str,
+        *,
+        coordinate: Literal["response", "absolute"] = "response",
+        min_rows: int = 1,
+        aux_layer_ids: tuple[int, ...] = (),
+        hidden_layout: str | None = None,
+    ) -> HiddenStateCapturePlan:
+        if coordinate == "response":
+            offset = prompt_len - 1
+        elif coordinate == "absolute":
+            offset = 0
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unknown hidden-state coordinate: {coordinate}")
+        return cls(
+            request_id=request_id,
+            prompt_len=prompt_len,
+            window_start_abs=start + offset,
+            window_end_abs=end + offset,
+            collection_id=collection_id,
+            min_rows=min_rows,
+            aux_layer_ids=aux_layer_ids,
+            hidden_layout=hidden_layout or ("aux_final" if aux_layer_ids else "final"),
+        )
+
+
+def hidden_state_capture_capability(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> str | None:
+    """Return a reason when row-to-position mapping is not supported."""
+    if vllm_config.device_config.device_type != "cuda":
+        return "only the CUDA GPU model runners have a capture adapter"
+    if vllm_config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling:
+        return "async scheduling can reorder in-flight hidden rows"
+    if vllm_config.parallel_config.prefill_context_parallel_size > 1:
+        return "prefill context parallelism changes hidden-row ownership"
+    if vllm_config.parallel_config.decode_context_parallel_size > 1:
+        return "decode context parallelism changes hidden-row ownership"
+    if vllm_config.model_config.is_encoder_decoder:
+        return "encoder-decoder hidden positions need a separate mapping"
+    if (
+        vllm_config.speculative_config is not None
+        and vllm_config.speculative_config.enable_adaptive_verification
+    ):
+        return "adaptive verification changes GPU-side token row allocation"
+    return None
+
+
+def validate_hidden_state_capture(
+    plan: HiddenStateCapturePlan,
+    request: EngineCoreRequest,
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+) -> None:
+    """Validate a capture plan before assigning the internal request ID."""
+    from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+    from vllm.utils import length_from_prompt_token_ids_or_embeds
+
+    params = request.params
+
+    if not isinstance(params, SamplingParams) or params.n != 1:
+        raise ValueError("Hidden-state capture requires a single completion")
+    if params.stop:
+        raise ValueError("Hidden-state capture does not support stop strings")
+    prompt_len = length_from_prompt_token_ids_or_embeds(
+        request.prompt_token_ids, request.prompt_embeds
+    )
+    if plan.prompt_len != prompt_len or plan.request_id != request.request_id:
+        raise ValueError("Hidden-state capture plan does not match the request")
+    if reason := hidden_state_capture_capability(vllm_config):
+        raise ValueError(f"Hidden-state capture unavailable: {reason}")
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HiddenStateCaptureChunk:
+    positions: np.ndarray
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor
+    copied_bytes: int = 0
+    copy_ms: float = 0.0
+
+    def accepted(self, start: int, end: int) -> HiddenStateCaptureChunk:
+        keep = (self.positions >= start) & (self.positions < end)
+        return HiddenStateCaptureChunk(
+            self.positions[keep],
+            self.hidden_states[torch.from_numpy(keep)],
+            self.copied_bytes,
+            self.copy_ms,
+        )
+
+
+def drop_incompatible_aux_plans(
+    plans: dict[str, HiddenStateCapturePlan],
+    req_ids: list[str],
+    available_layer_ids: tuple[int, ...],
+    aux_hidden_states: list[torch.Tensor] | None,
+) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Disable captures whose requested auxiliary layout cannot be produced."""
+    errors: dict[str, str] = {}
+    for req_id in req_ids:
+        plan = plans.get(req_id)
+        if plan is None or not plan.aux_layer_ids:
+            continue
+        if (
+            aux_hidden_states is None
+            or plan.aux_layer_ids != available_layer_ids
+            or len(aux_hidden_states) != len(available_layer_ids)
+        ):
+            plans.pop(req_id)
+            errors[req_id] = "aux_layers_unavailable"
+    return errors
+
+
+def capture_scheduled_hidden_states(
+    plans: dict[str, HiddenStateCapturePlan],
+    req_ids: list[str],
+    num_scheduled_tokens: dict[str, int],
+    num_computed_tokens: dict[str, int],
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    aux_hidden_states: list[torch.Tensor] | None = None,
+    query_start_loc: np.ndarray | None = None,
+    *,
+    non_blocking: bool = False,
+) -> dict[str, HiddenStateCaptureChunk]:
+    """Copy scheduled window rows, optionally deferring completion to the runner.
+
+    With non_blocking=True, the caller must synchronize the current CUDA stream
+    before reading or serializing returned CPU tensors. copy_ms then measures
+    host submission time rather than completion time.
+    """
+    chunks: dict[str, HiddenStateCaptureChunk] = {}
+    row_offset = 0
+    for index, req_id in enumerate(req_ids):
+        num_rows = num_scheduled_tokens[req_id]
+        if query_start_loc is not None:
+            row_offset = int(query_start_loc[index])
+            if int(query_start_loc[index + 1]) - row_offset != num_rows:
+                raise ValueError("Scheduled hidden-state row boundaries do not match")
+        plan = plans.get(req_id)
+        if plan is not None:
+            start = num_computed_tokens[req_id]
+            first = max(start, plan.window_start_abs)
+            end = min(start + num_rows, plan.window_end_abs)
+            if first < end:
+                first_row = row_offset + first - start
+                end_row = row_offset + end - start
+                if plan.aux_layer_ids:
+                    if aux_hidden_states is None or len(aux_hidden_states) != len(
+                        plan.aux_layer_ids
+                    ):
+                        raise ValueError(
+                            "Requested auxiliary hidden layers are unavailable"
+                        )
+                    parts = [state[first_row:end_row] for state in aux_hidden_states]
+                    if plan.hidden_layout != "dflash_aux":
+                        parts.append(hidden_states[first_row:end_row])
+                    states = torch.cat(parts, dim=-1)
+                else:
+                    states = hidden_states[first_row:end_row]
+                copy_started = perf_counter()
+                if non_blocking and states.device.type == "cuda":
+                    cpu_states = torch.empty_like(states, device="cpu", pin_memory=True)
+                    cpu_states.copy_(states.detach(), non_blocking=True)
+                else:
+                    cpu_states = states.detach().to("cpu")
+                chunks[req_id] = HiddenStateCaptureChunk(
+                    positions=np.arange(first, end, dtype=np.int64),
+                    hidden_states=cpu_states,
+                    copied_bytes=(
+                        states.numel() * states.element_size()
+                        if states.device.type != "cpu"
+                        else 0
+                    ),
+                    copy_ms=(
+                        (perf_counter() - copy_started) * 1000
+                        if states.device.type != "cpu"
+                        else 0.0
+                    ),
+                )
+        row_offset += num_rows
+    return chunks
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HiddenStateCaptureResult:
+    hidden_positions: np.ndarray
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor
+    hidden_position_start: int
+    hidden_position_end: int
+    hidden_window_start: int
+    hidden_window_end: int
+    hidden_layout: str
+    layer_ids: tuple[int, ...]
+    includes_final_layer: bool
+    request_id: str
+    collection_id: str
+    copied_bytes: int = 0
+    copy_ms: float = 0.0
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HiddenStateCaptureBuffer:
+    plan: HiddenStateCapturePlan
+    chunks: list[HiddenStateCaptureChunk] = field(default_factory=list)
+    copied_bytes: int = 0
+    copy_ms: float = 0.0
+
+    def add(self, chunk: HiddenStateCaptureChunk) -> None:
+        self.copied_bytes += chunk.copied_bytes
+        self.copy_ms += chunk.copy_ms
+        if chunk.positions.size:
+            self.chunks.append(chunk)
+
+    def finish(self) -> HiddenStateCaptureResult | None:
+        if not self.chunks:
+            return None
+        positions = np.concatenate([chunk.positions for chunk in self.chunks])
+        states = torch.cat([chunk.hidden_states for chunk in self.chunks])
+        positions, unique_indices = np.unique(positions, return_index=True)
+        states = states[torch.from_numpy(unique_indices)]
+        if len(positions) < self.plan.min_rows:
+            return None
+        return HiddenStateCaptureResult(
+            hidden_positions=positions,
+            hidden_states=states,
+            hidden_position_start=int(positions.min()),
+            hidden_position_end=int(positions.max()) + 1,
+            hidden_window_start=self.plan.window_start_abs,
+            hidden_window_end=self.plan.window_end_abs,
+            hidden_layout=self.plan.hidden_layout,
+            layer_ids=self.plan.aux_layer_ids,
+            includes_final_layer=self.plan.hidden_layout != "dflash_aux",
+            request_id=self.plan.request_id,
+            collection_id=self.plan.collection_id,
+            copied_bytes=self.copied_bytes,
+            copy_ms=self.copy_ms,
+        )
+
+    def update(
+        self,
+        chunk: HiddenStateCaptureChunk | None,
+        accepted_start: int,
+        accepted_end: int,
+        *,
+        stopped: bool,
+        error: str | None = None,
+    ) -> tuple[HiddenStateCaptureResult | None, str | None]:
+        """Settle returned rows using accepted output progress."""
+        if error is not None:
+            return None, error
+        if chunk is not None:
+            self.add(chunk.accepted(accepted_start, accepted_end))
+        if not stopped and accepted_end < self.plan.window_end_abs:
+            return None, None
+        result = self.finish()
+        if result is not None:
+            return result, None
+        reason = (
+            "ended_before_window"
+            if stopped and accepted_end <= self.plan.window_start_abs
+            else "insufficient_rows"
+        )
+        return None, reason

[P2] Finalize capture when a stop string ends the request in the frontend

Capture is finalized in the scheduler only when its window completes or the scheduler observes the request stopping. A stop string is detected later in this output processor: it emits a finished response and aborts EngineCore. ## 第一性原理：审计所采用的必要契约

R1. 对 L 个 prompt token，第 j 个生成 token 由 h[L-1+j] 预测。因此 response [a,b) 对应 absolute [L-1+a,L-1+b)。这里返回的是预测该 response token 的 hidden state，不是消耗该 token 后的下一位置状态。RFC #56916 明确规定这一语义。
R2. 一个实际 forward 的第 i 个请求占用 query_start_loc[i:i+2] 指定的行，其绝对起点为该 forward 开始前的 computed token 数。必须先对所有请求推进 row offset，再按各自窗口取交集；不能按采集请求重新紧密编号。
R3. speculative forward 可以产生未被接受的候选 row。GPU 先按窗口复制，scheduler 再按实际交付的 token 区间过滤；同一 mask 必须用于 positions 和 states。
R4. CPU payload 可读必须晚于 D2H 完成，且 graph output 在覆盖前必须完成读取。MRV2 当前在 main stream 排队复制，output-copy stream wait_stream(main_stream) 后记录 event，get_output 同步 event，建立传递的 happens-before。blocking=True/False 不改变这个就绪契约。
R5. 每个请求独立拥有 plan/buffer；窗口完成和请求终止需要清理 worker plan。输出结果不得因为 DELTA coalescing、内部 ID 改写或 FINAL_ONLY 延迟而丢失。
R6. 校验对象必须是实际执行的参数；不支持的组合应明确拒绝或返回说明，不能先校验另一份参数再执行不兼容请求。
R7. copied_bytes/copy_ms 是提交或执行过的复制开销，不应因 row 后来被过滤、重算或没有新 token 而消失。有效 row 数和复制开销是不同指标。
R8. capture 未开启时不应引入无关调度、模型输出或全局等待策略变化；性能优化需要对应 feature-off 和 CPU 开销证据。

与 RFC 对照：响应坐标、半开窗口、稀疏 hidden_positions 为准、短样本/min_rows、request-local 状态等设计有合理依据。aux capture 只复用模型已有 speculative aux outputs，不能采任意未配置层；PCP/DCP、async scheduling、adaptive verification、encoder-decoder 均被拒绝。以上是支持范围，不是全组合通过证明。

frozen plan 防止同批请求共享计划后被原地重写；replace 是重新绑定 request_id 所需，而不是冗余复制大 tensor。
finished_hidden_capture_req_ids 与 finished_req_ids 生命周期不同：窗口可以在 generation 结束前完成；不能简单合并成只有 finished_req_ids。
query_start_loc 的验证防止 prompt-logprob batch 实际行边界错配；不能用“采集请求每请求一行”的假设替代。
accepted positions/state 同 mask、去重和显式 sparse positions 支持 speculative rejection、短结果与 replay；不要用连续 arange 填补实际缺失 row。
pinned CPU buffer + non_blocking copy 与 output event 传递同步是 Graph buffer reuse 正确性的必要组合；不能只删除 event wait 来换吞吐。
RequestOutput.add 的非空合并保证异步 collector 比消费端更快时早期 DELTA capture 不丢；直接覆盖为 None 会破坏该契约。

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Reviewed head `666bb57c72` with three reviewers (the current Codex model, Claude Opus 5.5, and Kimi K3), followed by cross-checking and CPU probes. The inline comments distinguish four correctness issues from test improvements and optional simplifications; I recommend addressing the correctness issues before merging.

Validation: 13 capture helper tests and 8 standalone preflight helper tests passed; completion and serialization suites reported 55 passing tests combined. The broader scheduler run had 201 passes and two GPU-environment-related failures; some output-processor tests were blocked by a gated model configuration returning HTTP 403. No real GPU hidden-state numerical, pipeline-parallel, or performance validation was completed. The pipeline issue was reproduced by driving the real scheduler with two scheduled prefill chunks before consuming their outputs, rather than by running a GPU PP deployment.

Contract clarification: the linked RFC #56916 allows partial windows and treats `hidden_positions` as authoritative. Partial results meeting `min_rows` are therefore not inherently a bug; please align the PR description's claim about avoiding partial captures with the intended API contract.

Threading request-local metadata through the API, engine, scheduler, and workers is justified. The simplification suggestions focus on duplicated state and capture-specific bookkeeping rather than removing necessary propagation.

Follow-up review of `6f9e63baaf`.

The source changes address the four issues from my previous review: capture completion now uses accepted output progress; stop strings and streaming input are explicitly rejected at admission; and auxiliary-layer errors are retained until a normal output is emitted. The scheduler regressions, CPU CI wiring, removal of the unused state enum, and extraction of buffer finalization are also improvements. This is source-level verification, not a claim that I reran the updated tests.

I would still like the following evidence and design alignment before approval:

1. **Validate actual model hidden-state values and token alignment.** The synthetic scheduler tests check bookkeeping, but cannot establish that either GPU runner selects the correct model rows and auxiliary layers. The standalone GPU script was removed without a replacement real-model numerical comparison. Please provide a small reference comparison and feature-off/mixed-batch coverage, including speculative rejection and pipeline parallelism where support is claimed. If that matrix cannot be validated yet, narrow the initially supported combinations.

2. **Quantify serving overhead.** `capture_scheduled_hidden_states` still performs a blocking `states.detach().to("cpu")` per capturing request per step. Please report comparable throughput, TTFT and ITL for the baseline, capture unused, and the periods before/during/after the window. RFC #56916 specifically asks for outside-window overhead measurements. The current `11 passed, 3 deselected` helper result does not establish numerical correctness or acceptable serving overhead; please identify the deselected tests and explain why they were excluded. I am not asserting a measured slowdown without benchmark data.

3. **Clarify the public API and related work.** #57663 implements part of the same RFC, and the RFC discussion already records coordination; #59543 provides a related per-request hidden-state output with a different scope. Please update the duplicate-work section with those relationships and explain which API/implementation pieces should be shared or remain separate. These are not interchangeable implementations, so this is an alignment request rather than a recommendation to close this PR as a duplicate. Engine/runner and completion API owners should review that contract. Please also restore the AI-assistance disclosure that was present in the previous description.

Optional cleanup: `HiddenStateCaptureBuffer.num_rows` appears to have no remaining callers after finalization was moved into `update()`. It can be removed if it is not intended as a supported API. Further simplification would be most useful through a smaller initial auxiliary-layer/execution-mode scope, rather than additional generic abstractions.

This pass followed the evidence-gathering gate in the requested review-pr workflow. DCO and pre-commit were passing at inspection, but the available checks did not establish GPU runtime validation. No tests, builds, benchmarks, or model evaluations were run in this follow-up; the earlier runtime results should not be treated as validation of this new head.
